_readme: Hand-written additions merged on top of the extracted rules data at load time.
Use this for content the upstream data is missing — most notably the class-specific
talent trees it references but never defines (Dark Side Devotee, Force Adept, Force Item,
Sith, Expert Pilot, Gunner, Knight's Resolve, Piracy, Military Tactics).
Add the talent itself under `features`, then list its id under the tree in `talentTrees`.
A tree stops being marked incomplete as soon as it has at least one talent.
Nothing here is validated against the books — it is whatever you type.
Icons: drop a file in public/icons/features/ (or classes/, weapons/) and name it here:
Only listed icons are rendered, so a missing file can never show as a broken image.
provenance: feature "superior-tech": requirements.levle -> requirements.level (prereq was never enforced)
49 species prerequisites retargeted from features -> species

Force Adept, Force Disciple and Sith Lord pointed at talent trees the source data never defined, while the trees they need sat unused under other names; those three were remapped. Without it those classes had no selectable talents at all.
12 Combined Feat rows hidden and rewritten as 8 entries in combos.json — they are automatic benefits, not selectable feats, and two of the eight had no row at all; see the note on them below
feature "attack-combo-fire-strike": a second copy of Attack Combo (Fire and Strike) under an "&" spelling; the stub is hidden and Soldier's bonus feats repointed at the full entry
9 prerequisite hints rewritten from the sheet's shorthand to the compendium's wording, now that the hint is the only copy shown; see the note on them below

49 Force techniques given the Force power each one modifies as a requirement; the books print no prerequisite line for a technique, but each states which power it changes -- see the note on them below
12 Force Regimens (Jedi Academy Training Manual) added by hand; the importer reads no regimen pack, so Force Regimen Mastery had nothing to grant -- see the note on them below
_comment_lightsaber_chain: Saga Edition has two separate chains. The Elite Trooper one in Weapon Master chooses a
weapon group and is correct as imported — nothing here touches it. The Jedi Knight one in
Duelist is lightsaber-only: Greater Weapon Specialization (lightsabers), CR p.218, whose
prerequisites are the other lightsaber talents and nothing else.
The import gave the Duelist entry the Elite Trooper talent's content: the name lost its
(lightsabers), the description was the generic 'choose a weapon group' text, specType made
it ask which group, and the prerequisites pointed at the generic ids, which the Jedi path
never grants. So a Jedi 7 / Jedi Knight 5 holding the whole lightsaber chain was told it
lacked Weapon Specialization and Greater Weapon Focus. Restored below to the real talent,
matching how its siblings weapon-specialization-lightsabers (CR p.41) and
greater-weapon-focus-lightsabers already read.
Juyo, Tràkata and Vaapad named the generic Weapon Specialization the same way, so the
lightsaber forms were shut too. They now name the lightsaber talent.
The Elite Trooper chain is not for lightsabers — that is what the Duelist tree is for.
Greater Weapon Specialization already listed the five groups without lightsabers, but its
tree-mate Greater Weapon Focus offered all seven, so an Elite Trooper could focus in
lightsabers and then never specialize. Both now offer the same five.
The Soldier's Weapon Specialization is deliberately left alone: it names no groups, only
any exotic weapon or group you are proficient with, so lightsabers belong on its list and
proficiency does the gating. Do not restrict it to match the Weapon Master five.
_comment_chosen_weapon: Critical Strike and Halt both say 'Weapon Focus (Chosen Weapon)', which the import read as
a matchingSpec requirement — Weapon Focus held with the very group being chosen. Neither
was given a specType, so there was never a group to match against and the check read
`!!spec && ...` with spec forever undefined: both feats were unselectable no matter what
the character had. They were the only two features in the data with a matchingSpec
requirement and no choice to satisfy it, and a test asserts that stays true, since a
re-import writes the pair again from the same wording.
Neither feat is actually tied to one group. Both effects use the same wording — Critical
Strike works 'while wielding a weapon for which you possess the Weapon Focus feat', and
Halt 'if you hit with an Attack of Opportunity, while wielding a weapon for which you
possess the Weapon Focus Feat'. That is every such weapon, not one chosen when the feat is
taken. So the requirement is simply Weapon Focus with no specialization named: hasFeature
matches any spec when none is given. One feat, no choice to make, and it covers each group
you have Focus in, including ones you focus in later.
The rest of each requirements block is repeated here because the supplement merge is a
shallow spread — naming `requirements` replaces the whole block, not just the one entry.
_comment_feat_prerequisites: A sweep of every feat's `requirements` against the prerequisite line the books give it.
The two disagree in fourteen places, and where they do the block is the one that is wrong:
`prerequisites` is quoted from the source, while `requirements` is parsed out of the
spreadsheet column by tools-import-excel.mjs and can pick up the wrong number, the wrong
ability, or a token belonging to the row above.
Blocks a legal character — the feat is greyed out for someone who qualifies:
savage-attack        required Vehicular Combat, which appears nowhere in the feat. Its
line is 'Double Attack (Chosen Weapon)' and its effect is 'one
weapon group or Exotic Weapon you have selected for the Double
Attack Feat', so the requirement is Double Attack held with the very
group being chosen — exactly how its sibling Triple Attack reads.
matchingWeaponGroupProficiency goes with it: Double Attack already
demands proficiency, and applied here it would also refuse the
Exotic Weapon case the effect names outright.
autofire-assault     both read 'Weapon Focus (Chosen Weapon)' and both were parsed as a
autofire-sweep       matchingWeaponGroupProficiency with no specType to satisfy it, so
the check was `!!spec && ...` with spec forever undefined and
neither feat could be taken by anybody. Same wording, same effect
('a weapon for which you possess the Weapon Focus Feat') and so the
same fix as critical-strike and halt above: Weapon Focus, no spec.
droidcraft           required Tech Specialist. Its own description quotes the line, and
it is 'Trained in Mechanics' and nothing else. Tech Specialist
belongs to vehicle-systems-expertise, whose line does name it.
angled-throw         asked for Strength 13 where the book says Dexterity 13 — a feat
about bouncing a grenade off a wall.
bantha-herder        all four say 'Base Attack Bonus +1' and all four were given +6.
gunnery-specialist   rancor-crush's own description quotes its line in full, and it
strafe               agrees with the prerequisite field against the block.
rancor-crush
Wrong skill, which blocks and admits the wrong people at once:
deadly-sniper        'Trained in Stealth'   was checked as Acrobatics
duck-and-cover       'Trained in Stealth'   was checked as Acrobatics
deceptive-drop       'Trained in Initiative' was checked as Acrobatics
vehicle-systems-expertise  'Trained in Mechanics' was checked as Pilot
Restriction present but never actually applied:
slammer              size 'small' against a ladder spelled 'Small', so indexOf gave -1
tool-frenzy          and the comparison passed for every size including Fine. Both mean
'Small size or larger'; powerful-charge already reads 'Medium'.
Their patch carries the appendage requirement as well and lives
with the droid hardware below — one entry per feat, since a
second entry for the same id would silently win over this one.
improved-sleight-of-hand  Dexterity 13 where the book says 15.
improved-bantha-rush      lost the 'Base Attack Bonus +1' its description still quotes.
Not checked at all, though the line is a plain feat, skill or ability name the schema
already expresses. These were reaching the UI as 'not enforced automatically', which is
the right treatment for 'proficient with weapon' or 'Receive the Gamemaster's Approval'
but not for these:
droid-hunter, unstoppable-force                    'Combat Reflexes'
fight-through-pain, officer-candidacy-training,    'Force Sensitivity, Trained in Use
rapid-reaction, recovering-surge                    the Force'
unwavering-resolve                                 'Trained in Perception'
power-blast                                        'Dex 13'
staggering-attack                                  'Sneak Attack or Rapid Shot or
Rapid Strike'
The rest of the unparsed set is left alone deliberately. 'Trained in at least one
Knowledge Skill' (recall) has no way to say 'any of these' in the schema, and 'Cannot be
a Droid' (instinctive-attack, instinctive-defense) has no way to say 'not'. Showing those
beats guessing at them.
The rest of each block is restated because the merge is a shallow spread — naming
`requirements` replaces all of it, not the one entry being corrected.
_comment_unobtainable_prerequisites: A prerequisite naming a feature nothing can ever grant is a locked door. Four ids were
in that state; three are fixed here and the fourth is left standing on purpose.
droid   The Droid trait gates fourteen features — Aiming Accuracy, Damage Conversion,
Distracting Droid, Droid Shield Mastery, Erratic Target, Logic Upgrade (Skill
Swap), Mechanical Martial Arts, Multi-Targeting, Pincer, Pinpoint Accuracy,
Sensor Link, Slammer, Tool Frenzy and Turn and Burn — and no droid had it. The
Droid species entry carries no traits, because a droid is built from a degree,
a size and systems rather than a fixed stat block, so `species.features` was
left empty and the trait was never granted to anybody. It is granted below.
`species` is merged over the generated species the same way features are; that
path was added for this, since species.json is rewritten by the importer.
Granting the trait is only half of it. Seven of those fourteen lines carry a
second condition about the chassis — '2+ Appendages', '2+ Tool Appendages',
'Claw or Hand Appendage', 'Hovering or Flying Locomotion', 'Hovering, Flying,
Wheeled, or Tracked Locomotion', 'Basic Processor', 'Shield Generator' — and
none of it was checked. Unlocking the trait on its own would have handed a
walking droid with no arms the Slammer feat, which is 'you slam a target with
your appendages'. Six are now checked through `requirements.droidSystems`,
against the systems fitted in the Droid panel.
Droid Shield Mastery is the seventh and is NOT checked: it wants a Shield
Generator, and the systems catalogue has no such entry — the nearest are the
Shield Expansion Module and the Micro Shield, and neither is the thing named.
Guessing at one would refuse a legal droid, so it carries the phrase in
`unparsedPrerequisites` and the UI says it is not enforced automatically.
duros   Spacer's Surge reads 'Duros', which is a species and not a trait. The
provenance note above records 49 such prerequisites already retargeted from
features to species; this one was missed.
skill-focus-initiative   Surprisingly Quick reads 'Skill Focus (Initiative)'. The id it
named is a summary-only stub trait ('Species trait. See your sourcebook'), not
the Skill Focus feat, so holding the feat never satisfied it. It is the feat
with the Initiative specialization.
intercept-starship-maneuver   NOT fixed. Telekinetic Vigilance (Zeison Sha Warrior)
requires the Intercept starship maneuver, and that requirement is correct. The
app carries all 27 maneuvers and has a slot kind, a picker filter and a derived
`starshipManeuvers` list for them, but nothing ever builds a maneuver slot — no
class offers the choice and Starship Tactics does not grant it — so no character
can hold one. Weakening the talent would be inventing a rule to paper over a
missing feature; the fix is to grant the slots.
_comment_exotic_weapons: Exotic Weapon Proficiency is 'Choose a single Exotic Weapon', but it was imported as a
weapon-*group* choice whose allowedSpecs were five weapon ids. Nothing resolves a weapon
id against the group table, so the picker listed the five as the raw slugs 'atlatl',
'amphistaff', 'bowcaster', 'cesta' and 'flamethrower' — and the other 28 exotic weapons
in the data could not be chosen at all.
The specialization is a weapon, so specType is 'weapon'. `specWeaponGroup` narrows the
list to the exotic group rather than naming the weapons here, so a re-import that adds an
exotic weapon puts it on offer without this file being touched. The spec values are
unchanged — weapon ids, which is what prereqs.ts already looks for when it checks
matchingWeaponProficiency against exotic-weapon-proficiency — so saved characters keep
_comment_stolen_form: Stolen Form hands over the talent it names, and nothing in the data said so. The talent
reads: 'Choose one Talent from the Lightsaber Forms Talent Tree; you gain the benefits of
this Talent and are considered to have this Talent for the purpose of satisfying
prerequisites.' Held only as stolen-form(ataru), no rule keyed on the form's own id could
fire — Ataru's Dexterity-for-Strength damage silently did nothing, and a later talent
wanting Juyo did not see it either.
`specGrants` says the chosen option is gained in its own right, and the engine adds it to
the resolved feature list. It is deliberately not set on the other ten features that
choose a feature: Force Power Mastery, Force Power Adept, Force Exertion, Focused Force
Talisman, Many Shades of the Force, Share Talent, Share Force Secret, Share Force
Technique, Coordinated Leadership and Squadron Maneuvers all qualify a power or talent you
already possess rather than granting one, and expanding those would hand out a second copy.
_comment_prerequisite_hints: The panel used to state a feat's prerequisites twice: once in the description, which the
compendium writes as a labelled paragraph ('Prerequisite: Dexterity 13'), and once in the
hint below it, which is the spreadsheet's own column. 109 feats carried both. The line is
cut from the description now and the hint is the only copy, so the hint has to be the
better of the two -- and for nine feats it was not, being the sheet's shorthand: 'BAB +1',
'Con 13', 'SF Knowledge (social sciences) or (galactic lore)', 'WP Heavy'. Worse, Sport
Hunter's read 'proficient with weapon' where the feat wants Weapon Proficiency (pistols)
or (rifles), which is not the same requirement at all.
Those nine are written out below in the compendium's wording, keeping anything the sheet
said that the description did not -- Shield Surge's scomp link, Sensor Link's associated
hardware. Only `prerequisites` is set, a string beside `requirements` rather than inside
it, so the shallow spread leaves the machine-checked block alone. Nothing here changes
what is enforced; `requirements` is what gates a pick and it is untouched.
The cut is not unconditional. It happens only where the hint covers what the line says,
compared on words with 'Feat' ignored -- the compendium writes 'Point-Blank Shot Feat'
where the sheet writes 'Point Blank Shot'. A hint that says less keeps both copies, which
is untidy and loses nothing, and is what a re-import introducing a new thin one will get.
_comment_force_techniques: Force techniques modify one named Force power, and now say so. A technique is offered by
Jedi Knight and Sith Apprentice, and every one of them below reads 'When you use the X
Force Power ...' -- Improved Force Lightning changes the activation time of Force
Lightning, Extended Force Grip its range, Cure Disease what Vital Transfer can treat. The
power itself was nowhere on the panel, so the list gave a player no way to tell which
techniques their suite could actually use from the ones that would do nothing.
The books print no Prerequisite line on a technique, so `prerequisites` is left alone and
only `requirements` is set: the technique is greyed rather than hidden in the picker, with
the power named under Requires and ticked once it is in the suite. The one the data already
had, Force Power Mastery, is untouched -- it chooses its power rather than naming one, and
Three name the power in the text rather than in the title: Detoxify Poison and Cure Disease
both modify Vital Transfer, and Dominate Mind modifies Mind Trick.
Force Power Mastery aside, seven techniques carry nothing. Force Point Recovery is about
Force Points, and Improved Force Trance, Improved Move Light Object, Improved Sense Force,
Improved Sense Surroundings, Improved Telepathy and Language Absorption improve aspects of
the Use the Force *skill*, which everyone trained in it has -- there is no power to
require. Add a technique here only when its text names a power in FEATURES; a new one that
does and is missed here fails a test in engine.test.ts.
_comment_force_regimens: The twelve Force Regimens from the Jedi Academy Training Manual, pp. 24-27, typed from the
book. Force Regimen Mastery has been in the data since the first import -- 'You learn a
number of Force Regimens equal to 1 + your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1)' -- but there was
nothing anywhere in the rules data for it to teach you, so the feat was selectable and did
nothing. Regimen Aptitude, the talent that gives +5 on the check to perform one, was in the
same position.
They are here rather than in features.json because the importer does not read them. The
Foundry system does ship a packs/force-regimens compendium (and a packs/force-regimes
beside it, which looks like a misspelled duplicate), but tools-import-foundry.mjs asks for
four packs and that is not one of them. Adding it there is the better fix the day someone
has the clone to hand: read the pack, drop this block, and keep whichever text is fuller.
Scan damage was repaired in passing -- 'dist ractions', 't raining remote', '{telekinetic]',
'a glass bottle of air'. creating' -- all of it spacing and punctuation, none of it a rule.
Two counts are left exactly as the book prints them because they read oddly and may well be
the book's own: the First Cadence wants 19 wax cylinders and 190 ball bearings, the Second
72 cylinders and 2,701.
No `page`: the section spans four pages and this text does not say which regimen sits on
which, and a made-up page number is worse than none on a panel that cites the book.
The five cadences are named '1st' to '5th' rather than 'First' to 'Fifth', which is how the
book spells them. Every list in the app orders features by name -- the picker and the chips
on the sheet both localeCompare -- and spelled out they sort Fifth, First, Fourth, Second,
Third, which is nonsense for five numbered exercises meant to be worked through in order.
Their ids still read `vorens-first-cadence`: an id is what a saved character stores, and
renaming one drops the pick out of any sheet that already holds it.
The feat carries a short lead-in above its own text. Regimens have rules that belong to
none of them individually -- one regimen's benefit at a time, benefits last 24 hours, a
failed regimen locks you out of that one for 24 hours, perform one whenever you have the
time -- and the feat is the only panel where a player meets them, since a regimen's entry
states just its check and its DCs. It is condensed from the section's four opening
paragraphs rather than quoted: the book's own wording repeats the feat's name and cites
the page it is printed on, which reads oddly on the feat's own panel.
The patch restates the description in full, because the merge is a shallow spread: naming
`description` replaces the whole array rather than adding to it, so the feat's four
original lines are repeated below the lead-in and a re-import that rewrites them needs
this block updated to match.

greater-weapon-specialization-lightsaber.name: Greater Weapon Specialization (lightsabers)
description: You gain a +2 bonus on melee damage rolls with Lightsabers. This bonus stacks with the bonus granted by the Weapon Specialization (Lightsabers) talent.
greater-weapon-specialization-lightsaber.prerequisites: Greater Weapon Focus (lightsabers), Weapon Focus (lightsabers) feat, Weapon Specialization (lightsabers).

attack-combo-fire-strike.hiddenReason: the same feat as Attack Combo (Fire and Strike), which has the full text

ion-shielding.prerequisites: Droid and Strength 13, or Cyborg Hybrid and Constitution 13

suppression-fire.prerequisites: Strength 13, Burst Fire, Weapon Proficiency (heavy weapons)

shield-surge.prerequisites: Droid or Cyborg Hybrid with a scomp link or similar, trained in Mechanics

elders-knowledge.prerequisites: Skill Focus (Knowledge [social sciences]) or Skill Focus (Knowledge [galactic lore])

sensor-link.prerequisites: Droid or Cyborg Hybrid with the associated hardware

awaken-force-sensitivity.name: Awaken Force Sensitivity
description: This training regimen is used to awaken another character to the larger world of Force sensitivity. You and the beneficiary of this regimen practice meditation, quieting your minds and listening to the Force. Time: 1 hour. Target: One willing ally who does not possess the Force Sensitivity feat.
Make a Use the Force check. The result of the check determines the benefits of the regimen:
DC 13: You gain the benefit of the Gauge Force Potential talent (if you do not already have it).

DC 18: As DC 13, and you awaken the first glimmers of Force sensitivity in the target. For the next 24 hours, the target can make untrained Use the Force checks as though he or she possesses the Force Sensitivity feat.
DC 23: As DC 18, except the target also gains a +1 Force bonus on Use the Force checks.
DC 28: As DC 18, except the student also gains a +2 Force bonus on Use the Force checks.

eyes-of-the-force.name: Eyes of the Force
description: This regimen trains you to sense images that you cannot normally see by reading the surface thoughts of others. During this regimen, an assistant holds a two-dimensional image viewer so that you see the images being displayed on the screen. As the image viewer cycles through different images of common objects, you must read the surface thoughts of the assistant to determine what image is being displayed on the screen at that time. Time: 1 hour. Target: You. Requirements: A two-dimensional image display and an assistant.
Make a Use the Force check. The result of the check determines the benefits of the regimen:
DC 13: You successfully read one-third of the assistant's surface thoughts. You gain a +1 Force bonus on Use the Force checks made to use the Telepathy application of the Use the Force skill.
DC 18: You successfully read two-thirds of the assistant's surface thoughts. You gain a +2 Force bonus on Use the Force checks made to use the Telepathy application of the Use the Force skill.

DC 23: You successfully read all of the assistant's surface thoughts. You gain a +2 Force bonus on Use the Force checks made to use the Telepathy application of the Use the Force skill. In addition, if you successfully use Telepathy against an unwilling target, you can also sense the target's surface emotions and stray thoughts (as determined by the Gamemaster).

oxygen-bottle.name: Oxygen Bottle
description: This difficult regimen trains you to master environmental manipulation through the Force. You must first empty a glass bottle of air, creating a perfect vacuum inside. Then you must allow only oxygen to slip past the seal created by the Force, eventually filling the bottle with pure oxygen before placing the vac-seal stopper. This regimen requires you to use the Force in a nearly molecular level, as well as the Sense aspect of the Force to determine what molecules are making their way into the bottle. Time: 1 hour. Target: You. Requirements: A glass bottle with a vac-seal stopper.
Make a Use the Force check. The result of the check determines the benefits of the regimen:

DC 26: You fail to create a vacuum in the bottle before the regimen begins, resulting in an imperfect mixture. You gain a +2 Force bonus to your Fortitude Defense against inhaled poisons and non-corrosive atmospheric hazards.

DC 32: You create a vacuum in the bottle, but let other molecules enter through your Force seal, creating an imperfect mixture. You gain a +5 Force bonus to your Fortitude Defense against inhaled poisons and non-corrosive atmospheric hazards.
DC 38: You complete this regimen perfectly, resulting in a bottle full of nothing but pure oxygen. You become immune to inhaled poisons and non-corrosive atmospheric hazards.

quiet-the-mind.name: Quiet the Mind
description: This regimen trains you to block out distractions and stray thoughts. It requires little more than finding a quiet, secluded spot and slipping into a meditative trance to clear your mind of doubt, questions, fear, and the chaos of the galaxy. Jedi use this technique to open themselves to the flow of the Force, allowing them to see distant places and events. Time: 1 hour. Target: You.
Make a Use the Force check. The result of the check determines the benefits of the regimen:
DC 13: You meditate, but your mind is still clouded by external stimuli. You can add one use of the farseeing power to your Force suite, but once it is used, it cannot be regained by any means.
DC 18: You meditate, quieting your mind except for but a few small distractions. You can add one use of the farseeing power to your Force suite.
DC 23: You meditate, quieting your mind entirely. You can add one use of the farseeing power to your Force suite, and you gain the benefits of the Visions talent (if you do not already know it).

telekinetic-practice.name: Telekinetic Practice
description: This regimen hones your skill with the Alter aspect of the Force and enhances telekinetic precision. You begin by placing a deep bowl on the ground, with an orb at the bottom of the bowl. First, you must use the Force to hold the bowl perfectly still and pin it to the ground. Then you roll the ball slowly up the side of the bowl, keeping it in contact with the bowl at all times, until it reaches the upper rim. The orb is then held in place for 5 minutes, and must remain perfectly still. You then roll the orb slowly back to the bottom of the bowl, moving it with the Force and not allowing the orb to move under gravity's power. Time: 1 hour. Target: You. Requirements: A deep bowl and a polished stone orb.
Make a Use the Force check. The result of the check determines the benefits of the regimen:
DC 18: You let the bowl move during the regimen. You gain 1 temporary Force Point which you can apply only to a Use the Force check to activate a power with the [telekinetic] descriptor.

DC 23: You let the orb roll under gravity's power back to its starting position. You gain 2 temporary Force Points which you can apply only to Use the Force checks to activate powers with the [telekinetic] descriptor.

DC 28: You complete the regimen perfectly. You gain 2 temporary Force Points which you can apply to Use the Force checks to activate powers with the [telekinetic] descriptor or use to reroll a Use the Force check made to activate a power with the [telekinetic] descriptor (you must keep the second result, even if it is worse).

sparring-practice.name: Sparring Practice
description: This simple regimen allows you to practice against another living opponent, simulating one-on-one combat. During sparring practice, each combatant attempts to strike the other while exercising restraint and control. If you use a training lightsaber (see page 56), you can spar without fear of harming your opponent. Time: 2 hours. Target: You. Requirements: Lightsaber (or training lightsaber) and a sparring partner.
Make a Use the Force check. The result of the check determines the benefits of the regimen:

DC 18: You hone your lightsaber skills but see little in the way of improvement. You can spend a Force Point to add to the result of a Use the Force check made to activate the Block talent. This does not count toward the "one Force Point per round" limit.

DC 23: You hone your lightsaber skills, improving your technique by small degrees. You can spend a Force Point to add to the result of a Use the Force check made to activate the Block talent. This does not count toward the "one Force Point per round" limit. You also gain 1 temporary Force Point, which can only be used to add to the result of a Use the Force check made to activate the Block talent.

DC 28: You hone your lightsaber skills and see significant improvement in your technique. You can spend a Force Point to add to the result of a Use the Force check made to activate the Block talent. This does not count toward the "one Force Point per round" limit. You also gain 2 temporary Force Points, which can only be used to add to the results of Use the Force checks made to activate the Block talent.

training-remote.name: Training Remote
description: You hone your skill at deflecting blaster bolts using your lightsaber. This Force regimen is performed blind, often with the help of a helmet equipped with an opaque blast shield. Time: 1 hour. Target: You. Requirements: Lightsaber, training remote, and a helmet with a blast shield.
Make a Use the Force check. The result of the check determines the benefits of the regimen:

DC 18: You hone your lightsaber skills, but the training remote gets several hits on you. You can spend a Force Point to add to the result of a Use the Force check made to activate the Deflect talent. This does not count toward the "one Force Point per round" limit.

DC 23: You hone your lightsaber skills, and the remote gets in a few small hits on you. You can spend a Force Point to add to the result of a Use the Force check made to activate the Deflect talent. This does not count toward the "one Force Point per round" limit. You also gain 1 temporary Force Point, which can only be used to add to the result of a Use the Force check made to activate the Deflect talent.

DC 28: You hone your lightsaber skills, and the remote never harms you. You can spend a Force Point to add to the result of a Use the Force check made to activate the Deflect talent. This does not count toward the "one Force Point per round" limit. You also gain 2 temporary Force Points, which can only be used to add to the results of Use the Force checks made to activate the Deflect talent.

vorens-first-cadence.name: Vo'ren's 1st Cadence
description: Vo'ren's first cadence teaches precision through control of one's body and sensory awareness. You set up 19 wax cylinders at 10-degree intervals around your body, each one approximately 1.5 meters away, forming a semicircle. Atop each cylinder, one metal ball bearing is placed. You must then use your lightsaber to strike each ball bearing without making contact with the wax cylinder beneath it. You must place the cylinders and ball bearings one at a time until all 19 have been placed. Time: 1 hour. Target: You. Requirements: Lightsaber, 19 wax cylinders, and 190 ball bearings.
Make a Use the Force check. You take a penalty on your Use the Force check equal to your Dark Side Score. The result of the check determines the benefits of the regimen:
DC 13: You damage two cylinders. You gain a +1 Force bonus to your Will Defense.
DC 18: You damage one cylinder. You gain a +2 Force bonus to your Will Defense.

DC 23: You complete the cadence without damaging any cylinders. You gain a +2 Force bonus to your Will Defense, and you gain the benefits of the Severing Strike talent (if you do not already know it).

vorens-second-cadence.name: Vo'ren's 2nd Cadence
description: Vo'ren's second cadence teaches not only control but also spatial awareness. You must set up 72 wax cylinders at 5-degree intervals around your body, each one approximately 1.5 meters away. Atop each cylinder, one metal ball bearing is placed. Like in the first cadence, you must place the cylinders and ball bearings one at a time until all 72 have been placed. However, unlike the first cadence, you must strike at all of the cylinders in a full 360-degree arc without turning your body to face the cylinders to the rear, honing your ability to strike at enemies coming from all sides. Time: 2 hours. Target: You. Requirement: Lightsaber, 72 wax cylinders, and 2,701 ball bearings.
Make a Use the Force check. You take a penalty on your Use the Force check equal to your Dark Side Score. The result of the check determines the benefits of the regimen:
DC 18: You damage two cylinders. You gain a +1 Force bonus on lightsaber attack rolls against creatures that flank you.
DC 23: You damage one cylinder. You gain a +2 Force bonus on lightsaber attack rolls against creatures that flank you.

DC 28: You complete the regimen without damaging the cylinders. You gain a +2 Force bonus on lightsaber attack rolls against creatures that flank you, and you gain the benefits of the Whirlwind Attack feat (if you do not already know it).

vorens-third-cadence.name: Vo'ren's 3rd Cadence
description: Vo'ren's third cadence teaches precision through control of one's body and sensory awareness. You set up 180 wax cylinders at 2-degree intervals around your body, each one approximately 1.5 meters away. Atop each cylinder, one metal ball bearing is placed. Unlike the second cadence, in the third cadence you must strike every fifth ball bearing, making a rotation around your body several times over the course of the regimen. This prepares you for irregular attack patterns from all sides. Time: 3 hours. Target: You. Requirements: Lightsaber, 180 wax cylinders, and 16,290 ball bearings.
Make a Use the Force check. You take a penalty on your Use the Force check equal to your Dark Side Score. The result of the check determines the benefits of the regimen:
DC 23: You damage two cylinders. You gain a +1 Force bonus on ranged attack rolls made when using the Redirect Shot talent.
DC 28: You damage one cylinder. You gain a +2 Force bonus on ranged attack rolls made when using the Redirect Shot talent.

DC 33: You complete the regimen without damaging the cylinders. You gain a +2 Force bonus on ranged attack rolls made when using the Redirect Shot talent, and you can spend Force Points to enhance Use the Force checks to Block and Deflect (as per the talents), even when it is not your turn. Furthermore, Force Points spent to enhance Use the Force checks to Block and Deflect do not count toward the "one Force Point per round" limit normally applied to spending Force Points.

vorens-fourth-cadence.name: Vo'ren's 4th Cadence
description: Vo'ren's fourth cadence teaches composure and quick thinking amid the chaos of battle. It begins by setting up 360 wax cylinders at 1-degree intervals around your body, each one approximately 1.5 meters away. No ball bearings are required for this cadence. You must strike the cylinders according to a complex mathematical formula. By the time the cadence is completed, you will have learned to perform incredibly taxing mental tasks while also focusing on the external chaos of combat. Time: 3 hours. Target: You. Requirements: Lightsaber and 360 wax cylinders.
Make a Use the Force check. You take a penalty on your Use the Force check equal to your Dark Side Score. The result of the check determines the benefits of the regimen:
DC 26: You make a mistake during the first hour. You gain a +1 Force bonus on Use the Force checks made to continue maintaining a Force power whenever you take damage.
DC 32: You make a mistake during the second hour. You gain a +2 Force bonus on Use the Force checks made to continue maintaining a Force power whenever you take damage.

DC 38: You make no mistakes during the regimen. You gain a +2 Force bonus on Use the Force checks made to continue maintaining a Force power whenever you take damage, and if you are damaged while maintaining a Force power, you can spend a Force Point as a reaction to not have to make a new Use the Force check.

vorens-fifth-cadence.name: Vo'ren's 5th Cadence
description: In Vo'ren's fifth and final cadence, you must demonstrate true mastery over yourself and your lightsaber. No wax cylinders are required; you simply know when you have made a correct strike. Unlike the other cadences, this regimen requires you to use the Force to manipulate your lightsaber, an act of pure telekinetic power in which your hands never touch the weapon. This technique brings together the Control, Sense, and Alter aspects of the Force into one training regimen. Time: 3 hours. Target: You. Requirement: Lightsaber.
Make a Use the Force check. You take a penalty on your Use the Force check equal to your Dark Side Score. The result of the check determines the benefits of the regimen:
DC 31: You make a mistake during the first hour. You gain a +1 bonus on Use the Force checks made to use the Move Light Object application of the skill.
DC 37: You make a mistake during the second hour. You gain a +2 bonus on Use the Force checks made to use the Move Light Object application of the skill.

DC 43: You complete the cadence without making a single mistake. You gain a +2 bonus on Use the Force checks made to use the Move Light Object application of the skill, and you add the Kinetic Combat Force power (see page 51 of the Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide) to your Force suite. Additionally, you can spend a Force Point to reroll any Use the Force check made to activate a Force power with the [telekinetic] descriptor, keeping the better result.

Force regimens are training techniques used to hone skills and enhance sensitivity to the Force. They are ritualistic exercises that Force-users can perform during their downtime to keep themselves at peak performance.

Most regimens are designed to focus on one particular aspect of Force training. The benefits of a Force regimen last for 24 hours, and only one Force regimen's effects can be active in a given 24-hour period.

For story purposes, you can perform as many regimens as you like; you only benefit from the first one performed, however. If you fail to complete a Force regimen, you cannot gain the benefits of that regimen for 24 hours, though you can attempt another Force regimen you know. You can use one any time you have enough spare time to do so.
You learn one or more Force Regimens, which you can use to enhance your regular training.
Prerequisites: Force Sensitivity, Trained in Use the Force
Effect: You learn a number of Force Regimens equal to 1 + your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1).

Special: You can take this Feat more than once. Each time you take this Feat, you learn a number of additional Force Regimens equal to 1 + your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). If your Wisdom modifier permanently increases, you immediately gain a number of Force Regimens equal to the number of Force Regimen Mastery Feats you have taken.

_comment_feat_combos: Combined Feats — the Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide's term for a pair of
feats that does something extra for anyone holding both. They are not feats: nothing is
chosen and no slot is spent, and the benefit stops the moment either half is changed away.
The compendium already carries each one's wording inside the description of the feats it
belongs to, under 'Additional <Feat> Effects', which is where combos.json copies it from.
The summary spreadsheets file each pair twice, once under each half, and each row names
only the *other* feat as its prerequisite. Imported as written they became twelve
selectable feats — two per pair — each costing a slot and each demanding half of what it
should: Dodge + Running Attack could be taken by anyone with Running Attack and no Dodge
at all. All twelve are hidden here, and the pairs are written out once each in combos.json,
where both halves are named and the engine turns them on by itself. There are eight, not
six: Cleave + Follow Through and Combat Reflexes + Return Fire state their effect in the
feats' own text but were in none of the spreadsheet rows, so they had no entry at all.
Those same two are printed by a second book, and combos.json lists both: Follow Through
(Jedi Academy Training Manual) and Return Fire (Legacy Era) each grant the interaction in
their own entry, with no reference back to KotOR. Allowing either book is enough.
Only `hidden` is set, so the merge's shallow spread leaves the rest of each row alone. A
character saved before this keeps the row it picked — hiding only governs what the pickers
offer from now on — and it reads as unsupported rather than vanishing.
attack-combo-fire-strike is a different problem with the same smell. It is the Legacy Era
feat Attack Combo (Fire and Strike), which IS a real feat with a real slot cost, arriving
a second time from the spreadsheets under an '&' spelling. The dedupe pass compares names
after punctuation is stripped but not '&' against 'and', and compares rules text, which
differs between a summary and the full entry — so the two never grouped. The summary stub
is hidden and Soldier's bonus feat list, which pointed at the stub, is pointed at the full
entry below. Its prerequisites are the same either way and the test on the '&' shorthand
still reads the stub, which is kept in the data rather than deleted.
_comment_mortar: Galaxy at War p.40 gives the Mortar Launcher four shells, and the Foundry entry for the
launcher even cross-references them — its seeAlso says "Mortar Shells". The shells
themselves are in none of the packs, so they are typed in here from
The launcher's own damage type is corrected to varies. Upstream says Slashing, which
cannot be right for a weapon that fires whatever shell you load — the same pack uses
Varies for the Espo Mortar and for the grenade launchers.
No size is given for a shell in the source, so none is set here rather than invented: size
is what decides whether a weapon needs two hands or counts as light.
Damage types follow the shell table's own TYPE column, which reads Energy for the frag
shell where the hand grenade of the same name is Slashing.
_comment_damage_gaps: Three weapons the compendium gives no damage attribute for, whose damage was only ever in
their prose. The recovered descriptions already carry the conditions — the Stokhli's
webbing acting as a Net, the Amphistaff's three forms — so only the numbers are added.
The stun flag is deliberately not set on these two. It renders as "stun setting" and
"Can be set to stun", which describes a blaster you can switch; these deal stun and
nothing else, so it is written into the damage line instead. damageType is nulled where
the line already names the types, so the label does not append a second one.
_comment_stun: Stun settings, harvested from swse.fandom.com — one page per weapon, since the batch API
silently truncates the later pages, and folding non-breaking spaces first because the
field is written 'Stun Setting:' with one. Of 245 weapons, 149 name a setting and 91 say
Ten weapons deal stun and nothing else and had no damage at all; their dice are written
into the damage line, as the Stokhli and Neuronic Whip already were, so no stun flag,
which would wrongly imply something switchable.
Forty-two can be switched between normal and stun as a Swift Action, so they carry
stun: true. Six of those hit harder on stun and carry stunDamage as well; the rest use
The ammunition-fed launchers are deliberately not flagged. Their stun line reads Varies,
meaning it depends which shell is loaded, not that the launcher itself has a setting.
